column1: # ci-pkg-times.tsv: seconds per package, the median "ok" time over the queue batches named below (packages none
# of them ran keep their earlier value). ci_shard.sh balances shards on it. <pkg> and its <pkg>#<label> entries are
# the split rows of a package in ci-splits.tsv: engine/rules 135/59/89/83 (366 s, four groups as of 11-28), testkit/
# conformance 72/78 (150 s), dirac/kgen 74/43 (117 s), bots/azmcts 55/20 (75 s), engine/effects 38/20 (58 s).
# 46151834294 (five-run medians). The refresh corrects weights that drifted since the 11-27 basis: the engine/rules
# whole call measured 236 s then and 132-145 s in four of these five batches (64 s in the fifth), and azredeal
# 80 -> 88, dirac/kgen 48 -> 74, server/host 108 -> 115, dirac/shadow 106 -> 121. Under the old weights the true
# per-shard work summed 278/363/427/351/421/376 s; these weights place every shard at 369-370 s.
# engine/rules' four entries carry the measured call order, recovered from the shard each entry ran on in each batch
# (whole on shard 0, #A on shard 3, #B and #C on shard 4 under the previous placement; the ok lines name the
# package, not the -run regex, so a size-sorted refresh cannot recover them, and the shard-4 pair keeps the call
# order #B over #C). ci-pkg-times.sh sorts a split package's ok lines largest-first into whole,#A,#B,#C, which
# would label #B's ~89 s as #A and #A's ~59 s as #C; keep these labelled values until ci.yml's split calls name
# themselves in their logs. testkit/conformance's two entries measure 72/78: the ManaBrew regex half is now the
# larger, so a size-sorted refresh would swap them too.
# re-apply the split rows above by hand).
